extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians preparing manuscripts for submission to Compositio Mathematica
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for preparing and formatting a research article for submission to the journal Compositio Mathematica, covering page layout, title page, abstract, main text, figures, bibliography, and author addresses. Focused on presentation and submission requirements rather than scientific content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page format
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers should be printed or typewritten on one side of the paper. If a hard copy is submitted, it should be clean, not a blurred photocopy. It should use a typeface no smaller than 10 pt and preferably 12 pt and have margins at least 3 cm wide.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit single-sided, legible hard copies if supplying paper; prefer 12 pt typeface; ensure margins are ≥3 cm. Avoid blurry photocopies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title selection and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Title. Choose the title with care. A good title will indicate what area of mathematics is discussed in the paper. Avoid using symbols or formulae in titles, as they may present problems in bibliographies and make your paper hard to locate in searches. For long titles, please provide (e.g., in parenthesis) a short, alternative title that can be used for the running header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer descriptive, searchable plain-language titles; do not include mathematical formulae or symbols. If title is long, give a short form for header/running head in parentheses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract length and content rules
rubrics_metrics.description: An English abstract of less than 200 words is required and should contain at least two sentences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract must be self-contained and must not include citations, footnotes or references to numbered equations, theorems, figures or tables. If possible, avoid complicated formulae or displayed equations. (Abstracts will appear in the free-access section of Cambridge Journals Online and be listed in MathSciNet, so clarity and self-containment are important.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification numbers and keywords
rubrics_metrics.description: Classification numbers and keywords. Please place these in the footer as shown on this page. At least one subject code is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the AMS Mathematics Subject Classification (http://www.ams.org/msc/) for appropriate codes and include at least one MSC code and relevant keywords in the footer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acknowledgements placement and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledgements. Short acknowledgements of grants and financial support can be included in a footnote on the title page; longer and general acknowledgements are better placed at the end of the paper following a header such as the one that begins this paragraph.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use footnote marks to associate individuals with supporting institutions. Instead, explain the relationships in a single footnote on the title page as shown in the example.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Introduction. An abstract should never be regarded as a part of the paper and is no substitute for a well-written introduction. Write the introduction so that it can be understood by a mathematician whose specialism is different from your own.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain what the paper is about, summarise the main results, and for longer papers explain the plan of the paper. Do not number the introductory section '0', or if you must do so, omit the number from the section header.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theorems, proofs and remarks formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Theorems, proofs and remarks. Please mark clearly (e.g. with a vertical space) the ending of a theorem (lemma, corollary, proposition), proof or remark (note, example, ...) so that it can be distinguished from the text that follows.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure visual separation after theorem/proof/remark environments so the end is unambiguous to the reader.

rubrics_metrics.name: Footnotes usage and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Footnotes. These should be avoided as far as possible, but if they must be included, they should be separated from the text by ruled horizontal lines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attaching footnote marks to formulae or symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Figures and photographs submission and formatting
rubrics_metrics.description: Please supply these electronically as individual .ps or .eps files, or as hard copy in a form suitable for scanning. Electronic figures can be supplied in colour, but will be displayed in colour only in the on-line version of the journal. Hard-copy figures should be submitted in duplicate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure figure lettering is typeset in the correct type (e.g., mathematical symbols italic) and in a size that will remain legible after reduction. Captions should always contain a short, descriptive text. Captions may be included in the .tex file or listed on a separate page at the end of the manuscript with corresponding figure numbers. Do not include the caption text within the figure image itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bibliography labeling and ordering
rubrics_metrics.description: The publications in the reference list should be formatted as demonstrated below. They should be labelled, if possible, with alphanumeric acronyms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form acronyms from the first few letters of a single author’s surname (or initials of multiple authors’ surnames) followed by the last two digits of the publication year and letters 'a', 'b', etc. to distinguish same-year works. Order references alphabetically according to these acronyms and follow the sample formatting for entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author names and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Each author name should appear at the end of the manuscript together with the address of that author (and e-mail address, if desired), as shown below. Authors at the same institution should thus have their address repeated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include institutional addresses and optionally current addresses and email addresses for each author; repeat addresses for multiple authors at the same institution rather than grouping names under a single address block.
